FINDING_ID: IM_F001
SEVERITY: 0.91
FLAW_CLASS: 4
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.79
DESCRIPTION: `self_diagnose()` is effectively disabled under the default configuration. It returns immediately while `current_round < 5`, but `DynamicManagementConfig.max_rounds` defaults to `5`, so a normal 5-round run only reaches round indices `0..4`. That means the Level 3 self-adaptive immune layer never executes in the standard regime it was added to protect.
PROPOSED_FIX: Remove the hard-coded `current_round < 5` gate and replace it with evidence-based guards tied to the actual metrics each self-check needs, or pass `max_rounds` into the monitor and ensure self-diagnosis can run before the final default round.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: IM_F002
SEVERITY: 0.88
FLAW_CLASS: 1
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.73
DESCRIPTION: `record_round()` persists only the initial detector diagnoses to `self._diagnoses`. It calls `self._diagnoses.extend(new_diagnoses)` before appending remediation-outcome diagnoses and self-diagnosis diagnoses, then returns without extending again. As a result, `all_diagnoses`, `has_critical`, and any history-based analysis silently miss those later immune events, including critical self-diagnosis outcomes.
PROPOSED_FIX: Build the full `new_diagnoses` list first, then append it to `self._diagnoses` once at the end of `record_round()`, or explicitly extend `self._diagnoses` with `verification_results` and `self_diags`.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: IM_F003
SEVERITY: 0.86
FLAW_CLASS: 1
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.84
DESCRIPTION: `_extended_p_pass_remediation()` treats cascade risk as a SOFT warning even though its own contract says “no contradictions, no cascade risk” are HARD convergence requirements. The final `hard_failures` filter only rejects `Adversarial:contradiction` and `Module:target_metric`, so a fix can proceed after the adversarial pass explicitly found `Adversarial:cascade`.
PROPOSED_FIX: Include `Adversarial:cascade` in `hard_failures`, or downgrade the documented contract if cascade risk is intentionally advisory. The current implementation and its stated safety model disagree.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: IM_F004
SEVERITY: 0.84
FLAW_CLASS: 2
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.67
DESCRIPTION: Vocab-saturation detection ignores the configured sustained-window parameter. `record_round()` hard-codes `len(self._vocab_growth_history) >= 3` and slices the last 3 rounds, while `DynamicManagementConfig.vocab_sustained_window` is defined as `5` and documented as the required duration. This makes the immune layer fire earlier than the live config says it should.
PROPOSED_FIX: Thread `vocab_sustained_window` into `DetectorHealthMonitor` and use it for both the minimum-history check and the lookback slice.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: IM_F005
SEVERITY: 0.80
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.71
DESCRIPTION: `check_dispatch_health()` can misclassify old dispatch blocks as false positives based on any later success by the same model. The test is `any(s > block_round for s in successes)`, so one later success can retroactively “validate” multiple earlier blocks even if the success was unrelated, happened much later, or followed a different intervention. The detector has no causal linkage between a specific block and a specific decomposed success.
PROPOSED_FIX: Record explicit block-to-success linkage metadata and only diagnose when the later success is the matched follow-up to that block. At minimum, require the success to be the next-round decomposed retry and consume each success for at most one prior block.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: IM_F006
SEVERITY: 0.74
FLAW_CLASS: 2
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.42
DESCRIPTION: `FailureHandler.detect_failure()` emits the wrong real-time event for format failures. In the `FORMAT` branch it calls `_emit_event(... event_type=ManagerEventType.MALFORMED ...)` and then returns `FailureType.FORMAT`. Downstream monitoring sees a malformed event even though recovery policy and failure typing treat it as a distinct format violation.
PROPOSED_FIX: Emit a dedicated `ManagerEventType.FORMAT` event in that branch, or otherwise make the event taxonomy match the returned `FailureType`.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: IM_F007
SEVERITY: 0.72
FLAW_CLASS: 1
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.69
DESCRIPTION: The low-success self-adjustment path violates its own “simplest sufficient” rule. When both windows can be widened, `self_diagnose()` tries `("both", new_stuck, new_mu)` before `stuck_only` or `mu_only`, and applies the first candidate that passes P-pass. That means the broadest intervention is preferred over narrower reversible changes whenever it is merely safe enough.
PROPOSED_FIX: Reverse the candidate order to try single-parameter adjustments first, or evaluate all approved candidates and choose the smallest safe change set.
VERIFIED: TRUE
